newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai OTC market gets private placement go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Thai OTC market gets private placement go ahead.

text.p: The Bangkok Stock Dealing Center (BSDC), which controls the secondary Over-the-Counter (OTC) market in Thailand, said on Tuesday it had received finance ministry approval to begin private placement dealing.

Somnuk Wiwatana, manager of the BSDC's listings department told Reuters trading in private placement shares, aimed at increasing listings and volumes on the sluggish market, would begin at the end of November.
Private placement trading would be restricted to large or institutional investors.

In a further boost to the market, General Finance and Securities Plc said it was in negotiation with Bank of Thailand officials to explore the possibility of listing its potential new bank on the secondary market.
General Finance was among three consortia whose applications for new commercial bank licences were approved by the cabinet, pending final finance ministry approval.
Somnuk said negotiations between the BSDC and General Finance began around six months ago and they saw no technical or legal difficulties preventing the new banks from listing.
Bank of Thailand restrictions prevent the three new banks in waiting from listing on the main board.

Since opening late last year the OTC market has struggled to make an impact on investors or companies because profitable trading, unlike that on the main board, is subject to 10-35 percent capital gains tax.
At present, there are only two firms listed on the OTC.
